title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Signing the Declaration, Lead Time and Late Acceptance
content:
## Signature by the shipper

Under Dangerous Goods Acceptance the declaration is the shipper's own document, and the shipper is the only party able to sign it. A review can begin on a declaration the shipper has signed and on no other: a declaration still awaiting signature, or one returned for correction, never opens a review. Whether a signed declaration exists is read from the declaration file of the acceptance.

## When a signed declaration is on time, late, or out of time

- **On time:** signed no later than the category's lead time in calendar days ahead of the ETD shown on the booking.
- **Late but still taken:** signed after that point, yet no later than the late-acceptance deadline of the booking's sailing.
- **Out of time:** signed after the late-acceptance deadline. Such a declaration is not taken for that sailing; the application remains submitted, and the shipper is free to withdraw it or to have the booking moved under the booking rules.

**The late-acceptance deadline** is the sailing's cargo cut-off time, as held on the booking record, less the category's late cut-off expressed in hours. Hours are whole 60-minute hours, reckoned in the local time of the port of loading, and a signature placed exactly at the deadline is still taken.

### Hypothetical boundary cases

The figures are invented for illustration. With an ETD of 2026-08-20 and a lead time of 4 days, a signature on 2026-08-16 is on time and one on 2026-08-17 is late. With a cargo cut-off of 2026-08-18 at 18:00 local time and a late cut-off of 30 hours, the deadline is 2026-08-17 at 12:00: a signature at 12:00 is taken, a signature at 12:01 is not.

## Charging a late declaration

The earlier provision under which a late but accepted declaration was charged the late declaration fee once, with a reference to the late submission, is **no longer in force**; the current basis for charging late declarations replaces it.

Two limits on that charge continue to apply. A late declaration fee may be entered only while the acceptance stands as submitted or under review. And one late submission never bears the charge more than a single time; the line's account entries for that submission are the evidence.

## Summary grid

| Signature placed | Taken for the sailing | Application afterwards |
|---|---|---|
| within the lead time | yes | can proceed to review |
| after the lead time, by the deadline | yes | can proceed to review |
| after the deadline | no | stays submitted |

superseded_clauses: A late but accepted declaration is charged late_declaration_fee_usd once, referencing the late submission;
